lines.text: God gives a man riches, wealth, and honor, but a stranger enjoys them instead of him.
A man with a hundred children and a long life is worse off than a widow if unsatisfied.
The stillborn child has more rest than the unsatisfied man, even if the man lives a thousand years twice over.
All a man's labor is for his mouth, yet his appetite is never satisfied, and the wandering of desire is better than what the eye sees.

wrong_details.wrong: the wandering of desire is better than what the eye sees
wrong_details.true: Better what the eye can see than the wandering of desire

lines.text: Man cannot contend with one stronger than he, and no one can tell him what will come after him.
